lessons.culture: All through Ramadan, Cairo families hold an عزومة (invitation) for iftar, and the meal starts at the Maghrib adhan with dates and water. The du'a ذَهَبَ الظَّمَأُ is said exactly as the Prophet (peace be upon him) said it, in every dialect, and he taught that whoever gives a fasting person his iftar gets the same reward (ثواب). To رمضان كريم Egyptians answer الله أكرم.

response.english: Yes, the bedding is very comfortable.

pair.english: Where is the bathroom?
What time do you want to wake up?

lessons.culture: In Egypt a guest who stays the night (المبيت) gets the best room and fresh bedding, and any talk of being a burden is waved away with البيت بيتك (our home is yours). Good night is تصبح على خير (to a woman تصبحي على خير), always answered وإنت من أهله.

exercises.prompt: Your host asks: "نمت كويس؟". Say yes, praise be to Allah.

too_formal.feedback: "نعم" sounds formal in Cairo; people say "أيوه".

exercises.tip: الحمد لله is the same in every dialect.

exercises.prompt: Your host says: "تصبح على خير". Reply.

too_formal.feedback: Understood, but the fixed Egyptian answer is "وإنت من أهله".

exercises.tip: To a woman: وإنتي من أهله.

exercises.prompt: Complete: "الحمام _____؟" (Where is the bathroom?)

too_formal.feedback: "أين" is written Arabic; Cairo says "فين", after the noun.

exercises.tip: In Egyptian the question word usually comes last: الحمام فين؟

exercises.prompt: Complete: "هصحيك على صلاة _____" (I will wake you up for the dawn prayer.)
exercises.tip: ج is said g in Cairo: el-fagr.

exercises.prompt: Translate into Egyptian: "Do you need anything else?" (to a man)

too_formal.feedback: Written Arabic; spoken Egyptian uses "حاجة" for "thing" and drops هل.

exercises.tip: To a woman: محتاجة حاجة تانية؟

exercises.prompt: Translate into Egyptian: "What time do you want to wake up?" (to a man)

too_formal.item: في أي ساعة تريد أن تستيقظ؟
too_formal.feedback: Written Arabic; Cairo says "عايز تصحى" and puts "كام" last.

exercises.tip: To a woman: عايزة تصحي الساعة كام؟

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means "Here are folded blankets in case you feel cold"?
exercises.answer: أهي بطاطين متطبقة لو حسيت بالبرد
accepted: أهي بطاطين متطبقة لو حسيت بالبرد
options: أهي بطاطين متطبقة لو حسيت بالبرد
exercises.tip: "بطاطين" is the Egyptian plural of بطانية.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means "Did you sleep well?"

too_formal.feedback: Written Arabic; Cairo says "نمت كويس؟".

exercises.tip: "كويس" = well / good.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order: "الفجر / على / هصحيك / صلاة"

too_formal.feedback: Correct but written; Egyptians say "هصحيك".

exercises.tip: "صحّى" = wake someone up; "صحي" = wake up yourself.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order: "مشكلة / عندنا / مفيش / هتبات / الليلادي"

too_formal.feedback: Written Arabic; Cairo says "هتبات" and "مفيش مشكلة".

exercises.tip: "بات" = to stay the night.

challenge.title: Hosting or Visiting: A Full Exchange
challenge.instructions: Write a short conversation where you either welcome a guest into your home from the door to the table, or visit someone else's home and take your leave at the end. Use at least one greeting-at-the-door phrase, one phrase about food or drink, and one closing or thanking phrase.
required_elements: a welcome phrase at the door (e.g. nawwartena / etfaddal odkhol)
an offer of food or drink (e.g. tishrabu eih)
a closing thanks or goodbye (e.g. teslam eedak / ma3a s-salaama)

dialogue.speaker: Layla
dialogue.english: Welcome Mona, please come in.

dialogue.speaker: Mona
dialogue.english: It is your light, I brought you some simple sweets.

dialogue.speaker: Layla
dialogue.arabic: ماكانش له لزوم! اقعدي ارتاحي، تشربي إيه؟
dialogue.transliteration: makansh leh lozoom! o2'odi ertaa7i, tishrabi eih?
dialogue.english: You did not have to! Sit and relax, what will you drink?

dialogue.speaker: Mona
dialogue.english: Coffee please, plain.

dialogue.speaker: Layla
dialogue.arabic: اتفضلي القهوة، وبعدها اتفضلي على السفرة، الأكل جاهز
dialogue.transliteration: etfaddali el-2ahwa, we-ba3daha etfaddali 3ala s-sufra, el-akl gaahez
dialogue.english: Here is your coffee, and after that come to the table, the food is ready.

dialogue.speaker: Mona
dialogue.arabic: تسلم إيدك يا ليلى، الأكل تحفة
dialogue.transliteration: teslam eedek ya Layla, el-akl to7fa
dialogue.english: Bless your hands, Layla, the food is wonderful.

dialogue.speaker: Layla
dialogue.english: May your table always be full, take more.

dialogue.speaker: Mona
dialogue.arabic: شبعت والله، بس لازم أمشي دلوقتي
dialogue.transliteration: shebe3t wallaahi, bass laazem amshi delwa2ti
dialogue.english: I am full honestly, but I must go now.

dialogue.speaker: Layla
dialogue.english: It is still early, wait a bit!

dialogue.speaker: Mona
dialogue.english: Thanks for the invitation, I had a great time.

dialogue.speaker: Layla
dialogue.english: Visit me again soon, goodbye.

dialogue.speaker: Mona
dialogue.english: God willing, God keep you.
